title: Renormalization Group Analysis of Pairing Instabilities in Nuclear Fermi Liquids
authors: Yang Xiao, Yixin Guo, Youngman Kim
abstract: A nuclear Fermi liquid exhibits competing pairing instabilities in different spin, isospin, and orbital channels. In a Fermi-surface renormalization group (RG) treatment, the channel that develops a pole first is determined not only by its tree-level attraction but also by its one-loop RG coefficient. We illustrate this mechanism in a minimal $S/P$-wave model. A spherical Fermi surface establishes the reference competition between the lowest even- and odd-parity interactions. Axial deformation changes the relevant Fermi-surface integrals and lifts the degeneracy between longitudinal and transverse $P$-wave components. In isospin-asymmetric matter, neutron--proton Fermi-momentum splitting restricts the simultaneous low-energy contribution of the two species and can terminate the $np$ running at finite threshold scales. Our calculations are intended as controlled one-loop RG illustrations rather than as quantitative nuclear-matter calculations. We show how the Fermi-surface geometry and composition can change the ordering of competing pairing instabilities.
summary: This theoretical work uses Renormalization Group techniques to map out which pairing instability dominates in a nuclear Fermi liquid under varying conditions. By analyzing the pole scale of competing channels, it shows that both the geometry of the Fermi surface and the asymmetry between neutron and proton populations dictate the superconducting state formed.
main_problem: The study determines which competing pairing instability develops first in a nuclear Fermi liquid, considering various spin, isospin, and orbital channels.
main_result: The dominant pairing channel is determined by the pole scale of the Renormalization Group (RG) flow; this selection depends critically on the Fermi surface geometry and the degree of neutron-proton asymmetry.
method: A Fermi-surface Renormalization Group (RG) treatment is employed, using one-loop corrections to determine the running couplings and the divergence scale ($\Lambda^*$) for different pairing channels.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a nuclear Fermi liquid, analyzed using a minimal S/P-wave interaction model. The analysis extends to include effects of axial deformation and neutron-proton momentum splitting.
key_observables: Pole scale ($\Lambda^*_A$) of the RG flow; competition boundary parameter $r_P$; running coupling constants for different channels (nn, pp, np).
important_parameters: Isospin asymmetry $\delta = (k_{F,n} - k_{F,p}) / k_{F0}$; deformation parameter $ eta_2$; initial coupling strengths ($g_A(\Lambda_0)$).
main_assumptions: The calculations are controlled one-loop RG illustrations and not quantitative nuclear matter predictions; the analysis uses minimal S/P-wave truncations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the spherical channel selection diagram based on $r_P$. Figure 2 illustrates competition on an axially deformed surface. Figure 3 maps the dominant pairing channel in the $(\delta, r_P)$ plane for six components.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the RG flow by first establishing the spherical benchmark (S vs P wave), then incorporating geometric effects via axial deformation ($ eta_2$), and finally analyzing the impact of isospin asymmetry ($\delta$) which introduces finite threshold scales for $np$ pairing.
why_interesting: While focused on nuclear physics, the methodology—using RG flow to determine the instability order among competing channels based on geometry and composition—is highly relevant to understanding phase transitions in strongly interacting quantum systems like ultracold Fermi gases (e.g., superfluidity onset).
